open_questions: His kit's make in any era: no endorsement, interview or catalogue entry was found. Footage of 2002 shows black lacquer shells and chrome; Sabian cymbals in the Solitaire Unraveling video (2002), Zildjian by 2014.
Two bass drums or a double pedal: the 2002 footage shows one bass drum's front head; the Songsterr tabs' continuous 16ths need two feet either way.
Triggers and samples on the kick: the records sound triggered and the band runs samples live, but no source read says so.
His own drumming influences by name: he named bands (Megadeth, Metallica, Slayer, Sacred Reich), not drummers; the drummer links here are inferred from the bands' line-ups of 1986-87.
Which tracks on Savior Sorrow (2006) to A Wonderful Life (2020) he played in the studio, and which the touring drummers did.
Find a drum magazine interview (Modern Drummer, DRUM!, Rhythm) for his own words on technique.
Read the XIII-era masks from photos with true colour: the 2002 footage is sepia (the video) or under red light (Fort Wayne).

identity.name: Skinny

persona.description: Mushroomhead's founder, drummer, producer and visual director, masked since the band's first show in 1993 so it would not be confused with the members' other Cleveland bands. Of the mask: 'The mask just unlocks so much. It allows the real self to emerge onstage', 'a little bit murder and a little bit Darth Vader'.
persona.costume: A new mask each album cycle ('you get a fresh sculpt done'), most carrying the band's X face. In 2002 (XX on Universal, Ozzfest): a close-fitting black hood over the whole head with the X face in white and thick dreadlocks hanging from its crown down his back; a dark work jacket or the band's black tactical vest over urban camouflage, the 'masks-and-boiler suit' look.

identity.summary: Steve 'Skinny' Felton founded Mushroomhead in Cleveland in 1993, a masked side project of members of the city's metal bands that outlasted them all; he is its only constant member, its drummer to 2022 (in the studio since), producer of every record and director of most of its videos. A self-taught thrash fan who started at sixteen, he drives an eight- or nine-piece band of two singers, samples and turntables with down-tuned nu-metal syncopation, half time, 16th double bass, and the four-on-the-floor of the Rotterdam gabber he brought to the band. Since 2006 he has also played the lit water drums he built for the show.

traditions.impact: '86, 87, really wanted to become a metal drummer. I was into bands like Megadeth, Metallica, Slayer, Sacred Reich.' 'Back then I had big hopes and dreams that we'd be Metallica one day.'
'Got my first drum set when I was 16, I was a late starter, never took a lesson, taught myself everything'; one of the first things he had to learn was to hit a cymbal hard without breaking it.

'I'll bring like the hardcore gabber type techno ideas ... abrasive, 180 beats a minute': Nightmare in Rotterdam, early Thunderdome; the band ended its home shows with a hardcore mix set. Heard as the four-on-the-floor under Bwomp.

evidence.note: From automatic captions of an audio interview.

traditions.impact: Kiss (Cobo Hall, late 1970s), Alice Cooper, Bowie, the Residents ('There's no rules, you can do anything'), Mr. Bungle and Pink Floyd's The Wall shaped the masks, the visuals and the cinematic records rather than the drumming.

formative_events.event: Founded Mushroomhead in Cleveland's Warehouse District as a masked side project; its first show at a club, and three days later in front of 2,000 at the Cleveland Agora with GWAR.
XX, songs from the three self-released albums, on Eclipse and then Universal; Ozzfest 2002.
Water drums added to the show: built with Cleveland designer Dave Brooks for an intermission piece of his own, 'a drum solo but not on a drum set', after the Blue Man Group.
Back injuries took him off the live kit; he plays water drums, keyboards and samples live and the drums in the studio.

dynamics.balance: A loud kick ('almost as loud as the voice or guitars'), a backbeat snare, open hats and crashes; almost no ghost notes in the tabs.

feel_profile.interaction: Locks the kick to the down-tuned riff and plays under samples, keyboards and turntables; half-time sections and stops follow the guitars.

hand_techniques.name: Open hat on the off-beats and quarters
hand_techniques.description: A washy open hat on the quarters in half-time sections (Solitaire Unraveling, Kill Tomorrow) or on every eighth but the first under a syncopated kick (Sun Doesn't Rise's verse), the crash on the 1.

hand_techniques.name: Half time
hand_techniques.description: The snare on 3 under riffs at 140 to 160, the kick on syncopated eighths.

hand_techniques.name: Tom intros in 16ths
hand_techniques.description: Song intros on a single tom in 16ths, two on and one off or straight, with the kick under them (Sun Doesn't Rise on the mid tom, Before I Die on the floor tom).

hand_techniques.name: Cymbal bashing
hand_techniques.description: Hits cymbals hard, a technique he says he had to learn so as not to break them; a ring of a dozen cymbals with two chinas and two hats.

foot_techniques.name: 16th double bass under the backbeat
foot_techniques.description: Continuous 16ths on the bass drums under open quarter hats and a snare on 2 and 4, at 140 (Kill Tomorrow) and 160 (Before I Die).

foot_techniques.name: Syncopated kick on the riff
foot_techniques.description: The kick in dotted eighths and 16th pickups following the guitar (Sun Doesn't Rise), or in a burst of four 16ths on the beat (Bwomp).

foot_techniques.name: Four on the floor
foot_techniques.description: The kick on every beat under 16th hats in the techno sections, from the gabber he brought to the band.

devices_search.note: None found. Sun Doesn't Rise's kick runs in dotted eighths (16th steps 0, 3, 6, 9) then 11 and 13 under a steady backbeat: a riff figure inside one bar that resolves to the next 1, no cross pulse held against the meter. The half-time bars, 16th double bass and four-on-the-floor are feel and speed. No odd meter in the tabs read.

voice_language.hihat: Open and washy, on the quarters or the off-beat eighths; closed 16ths in the techno sections.
voice_language.snare: Backbeat on 2 and 4, or on 3 in half time; a 16th pickup before the next bar.
voice_language.kick: On the riff in syncopated eighths and 16ths; continuous 16th double bass in the heaviest parts; four on the floor under techno.
voice_language.toms: Intros on one tom in 16ths; rack toms in a row across the bass drum.
voice_language.cymbals: A crash on the 1 of each phrase, chinas at each side, two hi-hats, a ride bell in the middle.

implements.notes: The water drums are played with sticks too.

aesthetic: loud, punchy kick at the front of the mix
big wash of crashes and chinas
drums against samples, keyboards and turntables

sample_hints.2003: Modern metal kit: punchy, clicky kick, tight high snare, big crashes and chinas, close-miked.

signature_traits.label: The kick on the riff
signature_traits.description: Syncopated kick figures that double the down-tuned guitar under a plain backbeat and an open hat: Sun Doesn't Rise's dotted eighths, Solitaire Unraveling's half time.

signature_traits.label: Double bass under a backbeat
signature_traits.description: Continuous 16th double bass under open quarter hats and the snare on 2 and 4 for the heaviest sections.

signature_traits.label: Techno inside metal
signature_traits.description: Brought Rotterdam gabber and hardcore techno to the band: the four-on-the-floor kick under 16th hats in Bwomp's techno sections.

signature_traits.label: Masked, and the band's director
signature_traits.description: Plays in a full-head mask with no peripheral vision ('We have a lot of hand signals because there's no lip reading'); founded the band, produces the records and designs the masks and videos.

signature_traits.label: Water drums
signature_traits.description: Lit drums with water on their heads that splash as they are struck, built with Dave Brooks after the Blue Man Group for a piece of his own, then a set piece for the band's percussionists.

Mushroomhead's water drummer and touring drummer beside him.

philosophy.idea: Hitting a cymbal hard without breaking it takes finesse and technique; breaking them is not cool.
The drums are the heart of the live show, and in metal now they sit at the front of the song rather than behind it.

innovations: A masked metal band from 1993, years before the masked metal of the nu-metal boom
Gabber and hardcore techno inside alternative metal
Lit water drums as a metal set piece

cultural_references.description: The Mushroomhead-Slipknot rivalry, mostly fan-driven, from 1999; Felton now calls Slipknot 'amazing'.

common_misconceptions: That Mushroomhead copied Slipknot's masks: they wore them from 1993.

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: Modern metal kit: punchy kick, tight cracking snare, big crashes and chinas
generation_rules: Straight 16ths; no swing, almost no ghost notes.
Kick on the riff in syncopated eighths and 16ths under a plain backbeat.
Open hat on the quarters in half time, on the off-beat eighths elsewhere; crash on the 1 of each phrase.
Half-time sections with the snare on 3 at 140 to 160.
Continuous 16th double bass for the heaviest sections, alternating feet.
Four on the floor under 16th hats for the techno sections.
Fills short, at phrase ends: tom runs in 16ths, a snare pickup, a crash.

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: A self-taught Cleveland thrash fan of 1986 who added Rotterdam gabber, then put on a mask in 1993 and never took it off.
